blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Audio-visual instance segmentation (AVIS) segments and tracks individual sound-producing objects in videos. Existing benchmarks predominantly use monaural audio, which lacks inter-channel cues for spatially distinguishing concurrent sound sources. We introduce AVPS-360 (Audio-Visual Person Segmentation 360), a spatial audio-visual benchmark bridging AVIS and sound event localisation and detection (SELD). Built upon STARSS23, it pairs first-order Ambisonics audio with synchronised 360° video across 230 recordings totalling 10.5 hours. Recordings average 164.0 seconds. The dataset captures intermittent sound production in real-world interactions dominated by speech, alongside laughter, clapping, and footsteps. It provides 31,678 manually reviewed instance masks linked to source identities and sound-event labels. We also present a baseline that integrates spatial audio with visual features for frame-level segmentation and identity association across frames. Experiments on AVPS-360 show that existing AVIS methods struggle with detection and identity association in long recordings with intermittent sound production, while our baseline substantially improves performance in both aspects.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Vision and hearing help us associate sounds with the people around us and
follow their activities as they move and take turns speaking. For embodied
agents and assistive robots, similar awareness of the surrounding physical
environment could support interaction beyond a forward-facing camera’s view,
such as responding to someone calling from behind or alerting users to
activity outside their current view.

环境可以支持前视相机以外的相互作用,
例如对从背后打电话的人作出反应或提醒用户注意

blocks.en:
Audio-visual instance segmentation (AVIS) has established a foundation for
segmenting and tracking individual sound-producing objects through
AVISeg [ 4 ] , while AVTrack [ 5 ] extends evaluation
to complex human-centric scenes. However, these benchmarks primarily pair
perspective video with monaural audio and therefore do not jointly provide
panoramic visual context and inter-channel directional cues. General-purpose
audio-visual models such as Qwen3-Omni [ 6 ] likewise use monaural
audio in their standard input pipeline, without retaining inter-channel
directional cues.
Panoramic video
offers visual coverage beyond a single viewing direction, while spatial audio
provides directional evidence for determining which of several visible
persons are producing sound.

blocks.en:
Audio-visual sound event localisation and detection (SELD) datasets such as
STARSS23 [ 7 ] provide multichannel audio and panoramic
video, but their direction-of-arrival (DOA) annotations specify source
directions rather than person masks. Standard SELD evaluation also does not
require persistent identities across overlapping or intermittent
events [ 8 ] . Linking spatial sound-event annotations to
person masks and recording-level identities would connect acoustic scene
analysis with instance-level visual grounding and tracking.

blocks.en:
To connect these capabilities, we introduce AVPS-360 , built upon
STARSS23. It pairs four-channel first-order Ambisonics (FOA) audio with
synchronised 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} video across 230 recordings of average duration
164.0 seconds, totalling 10.5 hours. We provide 31,678 manually reviewed person masks
linked to recording-level identities and sound-event labels. The indoor
interactions are dominated by speech, alongside laughter, clapping, and
footsteps. Models must segment visible persons while they produce sound,
suppress their masks during silence even when they remain visible, and
preserve their identities when sound production resumes.

blocks.en:
We further establish a simple baseline that uses spatial audio to guide
frame-level instance segmentation and a memory of instance embeddings for
cross-frame identity association. Experiments demonstrate the benefits of
spatial audio and reveal substantial detection and association challenges for
existing AVIS methods on AVPS-360 .

blocks.en:
Our contributions are: (i) a spatial audio-visual dataset linking
first-order Ambisonics and panoramic video to person masks, source identities,
and sound-event labels; (ii) a benchmark for segmenting and tracking
intermittently sound-producing persons in long recordings; and (iii) a
baseline and comparative evaluation demonstrating the value of spatial audio
and the challenges faced by existing AVIS methods.
The dataset is publicly available through the project

released upon acceptance.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Audio-visual segmentation and instance tracking. Visual sound localisation identifies audible sources in images through
response heatmaps [ 9 , 10 ] . Audio-visual
segmentation (AVS) predicts pixel-level masks,
with AVSBench supporting binary and semantic
segmentation [ 1 , 2 ] and RefAVS-Bench adding language-guided
targets [ 3 ] .
For instance-level modelling, AVISM [ 4 ] combines frame-level
sound-source localisation with video-level object-token association.
Subsequent work investigates sound-source association [ 11 ] and
sound-enhanced online instance association [ 12 ] .
SAMOT [ 13 ] combines adaptive Mamba step modulation with
optimal transport for instance-level cross-modal matching.

blocks.en:
Sound event localisation and detection. SELD jointly identifies sound classes and estimates source directions from
multichannel audio [ 14 , 15 ] , including
simultaneously active sources of the same class [ 16 ] .
Source locations are represented by azimuth and elevation.
Audio-visual SELD incorporates visual cues into event detection and
localisation through audio-visual embedding fusion [ 17 ] and video-attention mechanisms [ 18 ] .

blocks.en: 3 The AVPS-360 Dataset
blocks.zh: 3 AVPS-360 数据集

blocks.en:
AVPS-360 is built on STARSS23 [ 7 ] , a dataset of
indoor sound scenes improvised by participants following general instructions
and recorded in 23 rooms with a spherical microphone array and a co-located 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} camera. It provides synchronised four-channel
first-order Ambisonics, equirectangular video at 1920 × 960 1920\times 960 pixels and
29.97 frames per second, and spatiotemporal sound-event annotations.
Visible faces are blurred in the released STARSS23 videos for participant
privacy [ 7 ] .
We keep the STARSS23 partition: its development set becomes our training split
and its evaluation set our test split, so no room or recording session is shared between
the two. A person track links the annotated masks of the same person throughout
one recording. The training split contains 156 recordings (7.06 h), 20,734 masks,
and 340 person tracks; the test split contains 74 recordings (3.42 h),
10,944 masks, and 168 person tracks. No separate validation split is used.

blocks.en: 3.1 Annotation
blocks.zh: 3.1 注释

blocks.en:
We annotate one video frame per second, yielding 37,718 annotated frames.
Each visible sound-producing person receives one mask per timestamp and retains
the same identity across sound-event classes; simultaneous event labels are allowed.
Regions of the same person split across the panoramic seam are annotated as
a single instance mask.
For heavily occluded persons whose visible regions cannot be reliably annotated,
we retain sound-event labels and source identities but omit masks.
These persons are treated as non-targets at those timestamps.
Fig. 1 shows sample frames.

不同声音类的相同身份;允许同时使用事件标签。

blocks.en:
We use SAM 3 [ 19 ] to segment visible persons and retain five
human-produced sound classes from STARSS23: female speech, male speech,
clapping, laughter, and footsteps. Projected DOA locations are matched to the
nearest mask centroids to assign source identities and sound-event labels.
Non-human sounds remain as acoustic distractors. All annotated frames undergo
multiple rounds of manual review, correction, and verification using ISAT 2 2 2 https://github.com/yatengLG/ISAT_with_segment_anything to
resolve segmentation errors and identity mismatches caused by source-location
offsets, movement, and occlusion.
Event categories are provided as metadata but are neither used for event-class
supervision nor predicted by the baseline.

blocks.en:
Evaluation metrics. Following AVIS and AVTrack [ 4 , 5 ] , we report
Track AP, HOTA, DetA, AssA, and IDF1.
Track AP evaluates instance mask trajectories using spatio-temporal IoU.
HOTA [ 23 ] combines detection (DetA) and association (AssA),
while IDF1 [ 24 ] measures identity consistency.

HOTA[23]结合了检测(DetA)和关联(Assa),
而以色列国防军1[24]衡量身份一致性。

blocks.en:
Implementation details. We train our baseline for 24,000 iterations with AdamW
on two NVIDIA GH200 GPUs, using a batch of two clips with ten frames
sampled from a 20-second window per clip. The initial learning rate is 10 − 4 10^{-4} ( 10 − 5 10^{-5} for both encoders), reduced by a factor of 0.1 at
16,000 iterations.
During training, we apply clip-consistent panoramic shifts, horizontal flips,
and visual colour jitter. The FOA audio undergoes matching rotations and
reflections.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced AVPS-360 , linking spatial audio and panoramic video to
sound-producing person masks, recording-level identities, and sound-event
labels. The benchmark supports segmentation and tracking during extended
interactions with intermittent target activity. Our baseline combines
audio-conditioned frame-level prediction with identity memory and outperforms
the evaluated AVIS methods on AVPS-360 . Under the same encoder
architecture and initialisation, FOA substantially outperforms W-only controls,
supporting the contribution of spatial acoustic information.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了AVPS-360,将空间音频和全景视频连接到
声音制作人口罩、录音级别身份和声音活动
标签。 基准支持扩展期间的分割和跟踪
与间歇性目标活动的互动。 我们的基线结合
带有身份内存和优异表现的音频条件帧水平预测
在AVPS-360上评估的AVIS方法。 在同一个编码器下
架构和初始化,FOA的绩效大大超过 只有W控制器,
支持空间声学信息的贡献。

blocks.en: 7 Compliance with Ethical Standards
blocks.zh: 7 遵守道德标准

blocks.en:
This study adds annotations to publicly released STARSS23
recordings [ 7 ] , without new participant recruitment
or data collection. The original study reports ethics approval and informed
consent for public release. We retain the face blurring in the released videos.
